# package usdo

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-canopen/usdo"
```

Package usdo implements the universal service data object (USDO) of CANopen FD (CiA 1301), which replaces the SDO: a [Client](#type-client) reads and writes the object dictionaries of \[Server]s over CAN FD frames, to one node, to a group or to all nodes, with several transfers at once.

CiA 1301 is a member document. This package implements what public sources establish and says where it had to interpret; the details below name their source.

#### Addressing (established) {#hdr-Addressing__established_}

A client sends on CAN-ID 600h + its own node-ID, a server answers on 580h + its node-ID: "CAN-ID identifies the sender", the destination is coded in the data (CiA's CANopen FD poster, 2026 edition, "Universal service data object" and "Pre-defined CAN-IDs"; a MicroControl CANopen FD master trace shows a request of client 7Fh on 67Fh). Byte 0 is the destination address: 00h broadcast, 01h..7Fh a node-ID, 80h..FFh a group (poster). A server answers with the client's node-ID as destination. Every client can address every server ("USDO mesh", Kvaser; HMS whitepaper). How a server learns its groups is not public ([WithGroups](#func-withgroups)).

#### Message layouts {#hdr-Message_layouts}

Byte 1 is the command specifier, byte 2 the session-ID, a transaction number with which a client tells its transfers apart (CiA "USDO protocol" page; poster). The command specifiers are those of the HMS/ Ixxat "Basics of the CANopen and CANopen FD protocol" whitepaper (local 01h..7Fh, remote 81h..FFh = local | 80h; see the Cmd constants). Layouts, bytes, with the confidence of each:

	upload request 11h, download expedited response 21h:
	  dest, cmd, session, sub-index, index (LE)                  established (MicroControl trace; HMS figure)
	download expedited request 01h, upload expedited response 31h:
	  … index, data type, size, data (8..63)                     established (poster; HMS figure)
	abort 7Fh: … index, abort code (1 byte)                      established (MicroControl trace "01 7F 01 01 00 10 12")
	bulk initiate request 06h: … index, data type, reserved,
	  size (8..11, LE)                                           established (poster; HMS figure)
	bulk initiate response 26h: … index, t_proc (6..7)           established, unit unknown ([WithTProcUnit])
	bulk segment 07h: dest, cmd, session, counter, data (4..63)  established (poster)
	bulk final 08h: dest, cmd, session, size of the last
	  segment, data (4..)                                        established (poster)
	bulk final response 28h: dest, cmd, session                  established (poster)
	segmented download/upload 02h/22h, 03h/23h, 04h/24h,
	  upload 32h, 13h, 33h, 34h                                  INFERRED, see below

The data type byte carries the low byte of the CANopen data type index (0: not given, an interpretation); the poster says size and data type let the receiver check consistency, so a server refuses a download whose non-zero data type differs from the object's with AbortLength. Multi-byte fields are little-endian as in all of CANopen (the trace shows the index so). Frames are padded with zeros to the next valid CAN FD length; receivers use the size fields.

#### Inferred: segmented transfers and counters {#hdr-Inferred__segmented_transfers_and_counters}

The public sources list the segmented command specifiers but show only the bulk layouts. This package uses, by analogy: the segmented initiate request 02h and upload initiate response 32h laid out as the bulk initiate request (size in bytes 8..11, no data); the initiate response 22h as 21h; segments 03h and 33h as 07h, last segments 04h and 34h as 08h; the end response 24h as 28h; the segment confirmation 23h and the upload segment request 13h as dest, cmd, session, counter (the segment confirmed or requested). Counters number the segments from 1, modulo 256 (the sources only say there is a counter, with abort 14h "invalid value in counter byte"). A repeated segment or segment request (the previous counter) is answered again rather than aborted. A client uploads segment by segment: request 13h with counter n, answer 33h with counter n, or 34h for the last. These are interpretations: they make this client and server interoperate, not necessarily other stacks.

#### Abort codes (established) {#hdr-Abort_codes__established_}

USDO abort codes are one byte (poster table "USDO abort codes"; MicroControl trace with 12h, timeout) — the HMS whitepaper's "4-byte abort code" contradicts both. [FromSDO](#func-fromsdo) and [AbortCode.SDO](#func-abortcode-sdo) map them to and from the classical codes with the same description; an [AbortError](#type-aborterror) unwraps to both.

#### Not implemented {#hdr-Not_implemented}

Remote (routed, 81h..FEh) services: their layout (network-IDs) is not public; a server ignores them ([ServerStats.Remote](#func-serverstats-remote)). Transfers of several objects in one service (announced for a later CiA 1301 edition). Segmented transfers to several servers: [Client.DownloadMulti](#func-client-downloadmulti) uses bulk transfer above MaxExpedited bytes, as CiA's example does. The client's timeout default (1 s) is this library's; MicroControl's stack uses 50 ms.

#### Services {#hdr-Services}

[Server](#type-server) and [Client](#type-client) follow the conventions of the other services: constructor with options ([WithLogger](#func-withlogger) ...), Start (subscribes before it returns), Close, Stats. A server runs one goroutine and any number of sessions (up to [WithMaxSessions](#func-withmaxsessions)); a client runs one dispatcher goroutine and transfers on the callers' goroutines.

## Types

### type AbortCode

```go
type AbortCode uint8
```

AbortCode is a USDO abort code: one byte (CiA's CANopen FD poster, table "USDO abort codes"; MicroControl's CANopen FD master documentation shows it as the 7th byte of an abort message, 12h for a timeout). It implements error.

```go
const (
	AbortUnknown       AbortCode = 0x10 // unknown error
	AbortProtocol      AbortCode = 0x11 // USDO protocol error detected
	AbortTimeout       AbortCode = 0x12 // USDO time out error
	AbortCommand       AbortCode = 0x13 // unknown command specifier
	AbortCounter       AbortCode = 0x14 // invalid value in counter byte (segmented protocol)
	AbortSize          AbortCode = 0x15 // incorrect data size
	AbortOutOfMemory   AbortCode = 0x16 // out of memory
	AbortRouting       AbortCode = 0x19 // USDO general routing error
	AbortDestNetwork   AbortCode = 0x1A // USDO destination network unknown
	AbortDestNode      AbortCode = 0x1B // USDO destination node unknown
	AbortSourceNetwork AbortCode = 0x1C // USDO source network unknown
	AbortSourceNode    AbortCode = 0x1D // USDO source node unknown
	AbortDLC           AbortCode = 0x1E // unexpected CAN DLC
	AbortMultiplexer   AbortCode = 0x1F // unexpected multiplexer
	AbortParallel      AbortCode = 0x20 // parallel USDO access to the very same sub-index
	AbortSession       AbortCode = 0x21 // session-ID wrong or unknown
	AbortWriteOnly     AbortCode = 0x31 // attempt to read a write only data element
	AbortReadOnly      AbortCode = 0x32 // attempt to write a read only data element
	AbortNoObject      AbortCode = 0x33 // data object does not exist in the object dictionary
	AbortNoSubIndex    AbortCode = 0x34 // sub-index does not exist
	AbortHardware      AbortCode = 0x35 // access failed due to a hardware error
	AbortLength        AbortCode = 0x36 // data type does not match, length of service parameter does not match
	AbortLengthHigh    AbortCode = 0x37 // ... length of service parameter too high
	AbortLengthLow     AbortCode = 0x38 // ... length of service parameter too low
	AbortInvalidValue  AbortCode = 0x40 // invalid value for parameter (download only)
	AbortValueHigh     AbortCode = 0x41 // value of parameter written too high (download only)
	AbortValueLow      AbortCode = 0x42 // value of parameter written too low (download only)
	AbortMaxLessMin    AbortCode = 0x43 // maximum value is less than minimum value
	AbortMinMoreMax    AbortCode = 0x44 // minimum value is higher than maximum value
	AbortCANIDReadOnly AbortCode = 0x45 // CAN-ID and CAN frame format are of access type read-only
	AbortNotMappable   AbortCode = 0x50 // data element cannot be mapped to the PDO
	AbortPDOLength     AbortCode = 0x51 // number and length of the mapped data elements would exceed the PDO length
	AbortNonMappable   AbortCode = 0x52 // attempt to map a nonmappable data element to a PDO
	AbortRPDOToTPDO    AbortCode = 0x53 // attempt to map a data element of PDO access type RPDO to a TPDO
	AbortTPDOToRPDO    AbortCode = 0x54 // attempt to map a data element of PDO access type TPDO to a RPDO
	AbortPDOValid      AbortCode = 0x55 // attempt to write to PDO parameters, while PDO is valid
	AbortMappingValid  AbortCode = 0x56 // attempt to write to PDO mapping parameters, while PDO mapping is valid
	AbortTransfer      AbortCode = 0x60 // data cannot be transferred or stored to the application
	AbortLocalControl  AbortCode = 0x61 // ... because of local control
	AbortDeviceState   AbortCode = 0x62 // ... because of the present device state
	AbortNoDictionary  AbortCode = 0x63 // object dictionary dynamic generation fails or no object dictionary is present
	AbortNoData        AbortCode = 0x64 // no data available
	AbortBusy          AbortCode = 0x70 // USDO server busy
)
```

USDO abort codes (CiA 1301, as CiA's CANopen FD poster lists them).

### type Client

```go
type Client struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Client is a USDO client (CiA 1301). Unlike a classical SDO client it needs no channel per server: requests go on 600h + the client's own node-ID with the destination in the message, and responses come on 580h + the server's node-ID with the client's node-ID as destination. Transfers are identified by a session-ID, so several can run at once, from several goroutines, to the same or to different servers. A transfer to a broadcast or group address collects the responses of all servers.

NewClient returns the USDO client of node (its node-ID: the CAN-ID of its requests is 600h + node). Call Start before transfers. Options: [WithLogger](#func-withlogger), [WithTimeout](#func-withtimeout), [WithBRS](#func-withbrs), [WithTProcUnit](#func-withtprocunit).

#### func (Client) Download

```go
func (c *Client) Download(ctx context.Context, server canopen.NodeID, index uint16, sub uint8, data []byte, opts ...CallOption) error
```

Download writes an object of a server: expedited up to MaxExpedited bytes, segmented (each segment confirmed) or, with [UseBulk](#func-usebulk), bulk (confirmed at the end) above.

#### func (Client) DownloadMulti

```go
func (c *Client) DownloadMulti(ctx context.Context, dest Address, index uint16, sub uint8, data []byte, opts ...CallOption) (map[canopen.NodeID]error, error)
```

DownloadMulti writes an object of every server dest addresses (broadcast, a group, or one node) and returns the outcome per server that answered: nil, or the error. Up to MaxExpedited bytes are sent expedited; more by bulk transfer (CiA's example of a broadcast bulk download): the servers that answer the initiate request take part, the segments are paced by the largest t\_proc they report, and each confirms or aborts at the end. Without [Expect](#func-expect) the call collects responses for the whole response timeout. The error is for the transfer as a whole (a send failure, the context).

#### func (Client) UploadMulti

```go
func (c *Client) UploadMulti(ctx context.Context, dest Address, index uint16, sub uint8, opts ...CallOption) (map[canopen.NodeID]Result, error)
```

UploadMulti reads an object of every server dest addresses and returns the outcome per server that answered. Expedited answers complete at once; segmented ones are continued with each server in turn, on the same session-ID. ### type Command

```go
type Command uint8
```

Command is a USDO command specifier (byte 1 of every USDO message). Local services use 01h..7Fh; the remote services (routing to another network segment) the same values with bit 7 set (81h..FFh).

```go
const (
	CmdDownloadExpedited   Command = 0x01 // download expedited request
	CmdDownloadInit        Command = 0x02 // download segmented initial request
	CmdDownloadSegment     Command = 0x03 // download segmented intermediate request (segment)
	CmdDownloadLast        Command = 0x04 // download segmented last request (end)
	CmdBulkInit            Command = 0x06 // download bulk transfer initial request
	CmdBulkSegment         Command = 0x07 // download bulk transfer segment
	CmdBulkLast            Command = 0x08 // download bulk transfer final
	CmdUpload              Command = 0x11 // upload request
	CmdUploadSegment       Command = 0x13 // upload segmented intermediate request (segment)
	CmdDownloadExpeditedOK Command = 0x21 // download expedited response
	CmdDownloadInitOK      Command = 0x22 // download segmented initial response
	CmdDownloadSegmentOK   Command = 0x23 // download segmented intermediate response (segment)
	CmdDownloadLastOK      Command = 0x24 // download segmented last response (end)
	CmdBulkInitOK          Command = 0x26 // download bulk transfer initial response
	CmdBulkLastOK          Command = 0x28 // download bulk transfer final response
	CmdUploadExpedited     Command = 0x31 // upload expedited response
	CmdUploadInit          Command = 0x32 // upload segmented initial response
	CmdUploadSegmentData   Command = 0x33 // upload segmented intermediate response (segment)
	CmdUploadLast          Command = 0x34 // upload segmented last response (end)
	CmdAbort               Command = 0x7F // USDO abort
	// CmdRemote is the bit that turns a local command specifier into the
	// remote one (81h..FFh).
	CmdRemote Command = 0x80
)
```

Command specifiers of the local services, as the HMS/Ixxat CANopen FD whitepaper lists them (table "USDO command specifiers").

### type Message

```go
type Message struct {
	Dest     Address
	Cmd      Command
	Session  uint8
	SubIndex uint8
	Index    uint16
	// DataType is the data type byte of expedited and initiate messages:
	// the low byte of the CANopen data type index, 0 when unspecified.
	DataType uint8
	// Size is the data size: of the data (expedited), of the whole
	// transfer (initiate), or of the last segment.
	Size uint32
	// Counter is the segment counter.
	Counter uint8
	// TProc is the server's processing time per segment of a bulk
	// transfer, in units the client and server agree on.
	TProc uint16
	// Abort is the abort code of an abort message.
	Abort AbortCode
	// Data is the application data of expedited messages and segments.
	Data []byte
}
```

Message is one USDO message (the payload of one CAN FD frame), decoded. Which fields are meaningful depends on the command (see the package documentation for the byte layouts).

#### func Decode

```go
func Decode(data []byte) (Message, error)
```

Decode decodes a USDO payload. Bytes beyond the message (CAN FD padding) are ignored. A payload shorter than 3 bytes, or shorter than its command needs, or with a size that exceeds the data, is an [canopen.ErrProtocol](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#ErrProtocol) error; an unknown command an ErrCommand error (with Dest, Cmd and Session set, so a server can answer with an abort). Remote commands are returned with only Dest, Cmd and Session set and the rest of the payload in Data: their layout is not public.

#### func (Message) Encode

```go
func (m Message) Encode() ([]byte, error)
```

Encode returns the payload of the message, not padded (see [Frame](#func-frame)). It fails for unknown or remote commands and for data that does not fit.

```go
func (m Message) String() string
```

String formats the message for logs.

### type Server

```go
type Server struct {

	// sessions are only used by the service goroutine (or a test calling
	// handle).

}
```

Server is a USDO server (CiA 1301): it serves an object dictionary to every USDO client of the network, several transfers at once, each identified by the client's node-ID and the session-ID. It receives on 601h..67Fh (client to server, CAN-ID 600h + client node-ID) the messages addressed to its node-ID, to broadcast (00h) and to its groups ([WithGroups](#func-withgroups)), and answers on 580h + its node-ID with the client's node-ID as destination.

Remote accesses go through [od.Dictionary.Read](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen/od#Dictionary.Read) and [od.Dictionary.Write](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen/od#Dictionary.Write), so access rights, limits and hooks apply; a refusal reaches the client as the USDO abort code of the dictionary's SDO abort code ([FromSDO](#func-fromsdo)). Downloads of more than MaxExpedited bytes are buffered and written once, when complete.

```go
func (s *Server) Start() error
```

Start resolves the node-ID ([WithNodeID](#func-withnodeid) or the dictionary's), subscribes to the client requests and starts serving. Once it returns no request is missed.

#### func (Server) Stats

```go
func (s *Server) Stats() ServerStats
```

Stats returns a snapshot of the counters.

### type ServerStats

```go
type ServerStats struct {
	Requests        uint64 `json:"requests"`        // messages addressed to the server while enabled
	Uploads         uint64 `json:"uploads"`         // uploads completed
	Downloads       uint64 `json:"downloads"`       // downloads completed
	Segmented       uint64 `json:"segmented"`       // segmented transfers completed (also counted above)
	Bulk            uint64 `json:"bulk"`            // bulk transfers completed (also counted in Downloads)
	BytesUploaded   uint64 `json:"bytesUploaded"`   // data bytes of completed uploads
	BytesDownloaded uint64 `json:"bytesDownloaded"` // data bytes of completed downloads
	AbortsSent      uint64 `json:"abortsSent"`      // aborts sent (refusals, protocol errors, timeouts)
	AbortsReceived  uint64 `json:"abortsReceived"`  // transfers the client aborted
	Timeouts        uint64 `json:"timeouts"`        // transfers aborted for inactivity
	Restarts        uint64 `json:"restarts"`        // sessions replaced by a new request with the same session-ID
	Busy            uint64 `json:"busy"`            // transfers refused: too many sessions
	Duplicates      uint64 `json:"duplicates"`      // repeated segments or segment requests answered again or ignored
	Remote          uint64 `json:"remote"`          // remote (routed) requests ignored: not supported
	Ignored         uint64 `json:"ignored"`         // messages ignored: malformed, from no valid node, while disabled
	SendErrors      uint64 `json:"sendErrors"`      // responses the bus failed to send
}
```

ServerStats counts what a [Server](#type-server) did.
